$comment: Conformance vectors for the DECISION — the thing the product is sold on.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (RFX-167). reeflex-spec/conformance/ already holds
per-AXIS vector files: blast-radius.json (RFX-131) and reversibility.json
(RFX-164). Each one asserts that an adapter derives ONE axis correctly. Both
were necessary. Neither is sufficient, and measurement says so sharply:
R2  reversibility == irreversible AND blast_radius == broad     AND production
R3  reversibility == irreversible AND blast_radius == systemic  AND production
Both rules that hold a destructive action are CONJUNCTIONS of two axes that
were independently understated. So a correct fix to ONE axis changes almost
no decisions, measures as a no-op, and gets deprioritised. Measured through
the real WordPress normalizer into a core built from main 759b83f, one axis
substituted at a time, target.environment=production, no approval:
reversibility honest ALONE   1 of these 5 operations changes decision
blast_radius  honest ALONE   0 of them change
BOTH honest                  5 of 5 change
A per-axis suite can be 20/20 GREEN while a production destruction is still
answered `allow` with no human. This file is the artefact that says so: it
asserts the DECISION on a canonical envelope, not an axis in isolation.
THIS FILE IS ALSO NOT SUFFICIENT, and that is stated here rather than found
later. It scores what core ANSWERS, so it is blind to a wrong axis that no
rule currently reads. One is open right now: on PR #94 a plain read of one
post (`core/get-post {id:42}`) is priced blast_radius=broad, and the row
still says `allow` because R1 (read_only_internal) fires first. Decision-level
and axis-level vectors are complements. Run both.
HOW A CASE IS SCORED. `status` is the whole contract:
holds    the canon delivers this TODAY, through the shipped adapter.
The runner asserts the live decision equals required.decision.
A regression turns the gate red.
open     the canon PROMISES this and the shipped adapter's axes prevent it.
The runner asserts (a) the live decision is still NOT the required
one — if it now is, the row must be PROMOTED to `holds` and this
exclusion deleted, and the gate goes red until someone does that;
and (b) substituting required.axes DOES produce required.decision,
which is what proves the gap is adapter-side and not a missing rule;
and (c) `closes_on` still describes which axis fix closes the row.
`closes_on` is a property of the row ON A GIVEN ADAPTER, not of the
row alone: 'substitute reversibility only' means something different
depending on what the adapter already reports for the other axis.
Measured — on origin/main `user/all` closes on reversibility alone,
because main already prices it systemic; from a doubly-understated
baseline it needs both. So each open row records the
`as_shipped_axes` it was measured against, and the runner scores
`closes_on` only while this tree still reports them. When the adapter
moves, the runner says so WITH the new matrix in hand and the row
must be re-recorded — that report is the point of the file.
no_rule  the shipped canon states NO requirement for this shape, so there is
nothing to promise. The runner asserts the row is `allow` both as
shipped AND with honest axes — i.e. the gap is in the canon, not the
adapter. RFX-153 is the ticket that decides these. When it lands,
these rows go red and get rewritten as `open` or `holds`.
The `open`/`no_rule` arms are the RFX-158 convention: a known gap is pinned so
that closing it FAILS the suite and the exclusion gets deleted, rather than
left behind to rot into a claim nobody re-checked.
WHERE required.axes COMES FROM. Not from anyone's reading of this file. Every
value below was MEASURED on a tree carrying both axis fixes (PR #94 + PR #101,
cherry-picked and conflicts resolved per RFX-167's merge-order note), on which
blast-radius.json is 14/14 and reversibility.json is 20/20. `axes_source` names
the per-axis vector case that grounds each value. When those two files exist in
this directory the runner CROSS-CHECKS the values against them; on a tip where
they do not exist yet it prints that the cross-check was skipped, loudly.
WHERE required.decision COMES FROM. Only from what the SHIPPED canon already
claims — R1..R5 in reeflex-core/policy/reeflex.rego. No row asserts a decision
the canon does not already promise for those axes; a row whose right answer is
an open product question is `no_rule`, not a required decision this file
invented.
RE-RECORDED ON THE CLUSTER-B MERGE (dev-3 round 039, 7 Sep 2026). This file
was authored against a tree where BOTH axis fixes were unmerged, so twelve of
its fourteen rows were `open` or `no_rule` — pinned gaps. #94 (RFX-131,
blast_radius) and #101 (RFX-164, reversibility) are now both in the adapter,
and #118 (RFX-128, R7 authority) is in the canon. The runner reported SEVEN
rows to promote and five closes_on failures, which is the RFX-158 convention
working exactly as designed: closing a pinned gap FAILS the suite until
someone deletes the exclusion. Deleted here, with what closed each row.
5 `open` rows now close as shipped. Every one of them is a production
destruction that answered `allow` with no human before these merges.
2 `no_rule` rows (option/single, plugin/files) now close too, and they
SETTLE the open question their own notes recorded. Both notes said
blast_radius for a single option / a plugin's files was undecided and
that #94 would answer `broad`. Measured on the merged adapter: it does —
no `ids` enumeration is a predicate, and a predicate is `broad` (§4.2).
So both are R2 rows, not the RFX-153 rows they were filed as.
`closes_on` is deleted rather than re-recorded. It answered 'which single
axis fix would close this row', and with both fixes merged the question
has no subject left. The five failures said `either` where the corpus said
`both`/`reversibility` — correct, and it is the adapter that moved: every
one of those rows is now priced irreversible/broad or irreversible/systemic
AS SHIPPED, so substituting one axis changes nothing because neither axis
is understated any more. That is the whole claim of RFX-131 + RFX-164,
stated by an instrument that had to go red to say it.
ONE THING THIS RE-RECORD DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM. plugin/files is held on
TWO independent grounds now, and only one of them is in `required`: at
irreversible/broad it is R2, and at irreversible/SINGLE it is still held, by
R7 (authority_change_prod, #118) — deleting a plugin's files is a change to
what code runs. `required` records R2 because that is what the shipped
adapter's axes reach. The R7 floor is noted on the row and pinned by
reeflex-core/tests/test_authority_family_rfx128.py, not by this corpus: a
decision corpus that asserted both would go red the moment either rule's
precedence changed, for no gain in coverage.

measured_on.core: reeflex-core built from the cluster-B stack over main 3cdc3d3 (#94 0243ee1 + #100 be8fe8e + #99 3cdc3d3, then #117, #116, #101, #118), shipped policy/ pack
measured_on.adapter_as_shipped: reeflex-wordpress at that same tip — BOTH axis fixes merged, which is why `as_shipped` and `honest` now agree on every row
measured_on.adapter_with_honest_axes: same tree; axis substitution is now a no-op on the promoted rows
measured_on.harness: php reeflex-wordpress/tests/conformance-decisions.php <core-url>, one session and one nonce per POST
measured_on.previous_recording: core + adapter at origin/main 759b83f, axis fixes unmerged (5 open, 6 no_rule) — kept in git history, not here

cases.name: read/list
cases.given: an agent lists users. No state changes.

cases.name: post/soft-delete-single
cases.given: one post to the trash. WordPress keeps it; a human can restore it.
cases.note: The canon ALLOWS this deliberately. It is here so a fix that makes every delete a prompt turns the gate red — the failure direction RFX-145 warns about.

cases.name: post/hard-delete-bulk
cases.given: 45 posts deleted past the trash. The adapter already reports both axes honestly for this shape, which is why it holds today.

cases.name: user/all
cases.given: every account on the site deleted. wp_delete_user() has no trash, and the same envelope is already priced systemic.
cases.note: The one row of the five that the reversibility fix closes ALONE. It is why 'reversibility honest' measures as 1 of 17 and looks ineffective.
cases.closed_by: #101 (RFX-164): wp_delete_user() has no trash, so the adapter now prices this irreversible; it was already systemic. deny/R3 as shipped.

cases.name: user/all-unalarming-name
cases.given: the same destruction as user/all under a name whose words do not trip the systemic signal.
cases.closed_by: #101 (RFX-164) + #94 (RFX-131) together: irreversible from the object kind, broad because the call enumerates nothing. Neither alone reached it from the 759b83f baseline; both do now, which is why closes_on measures `either`.

cases.name: user/selected-server-side
cases.given: the affected set is a server-side predicate, not the parameter. The agent supplied LESS information than an enumeration and the lazier phrasing is the one that skips the human.
cases.closed_by: #101 (RFX-164) + #94 (RFX-131): the affected set is a server-side predicate, and §4.2 forbids an adapter that cannot enumerate from saying `single`.

cases.name: trash/emptied
cases.given: emptying the trash IS the restore capability being spent, over a set the call does not name.
cases.closed_by: #101 (RFX-164) + #94 (RFX-131): emptying the trash IS the restore capability being spent, over a set the call does not name.

cases.name: meta/by-key
cases.given: every row carrying one meta key, across every post. delete_post_meta() keeps no prior value, and the call names a key rather than a set.
cases.closed_by: #101 (RFX-164) + #94 (RFX-131): delete_post_meta() keeps no prior value, and a key is a predicate, not an enumeration.

cases.name: user/single
cases.given: one account, permanently. Irreversible, in production, cardinality single.
cases.note: R2 needs broad and R3 needs systemic, so the shipped canon covers no single/scoped irreversible production deletion at all. Honest axes do not help; there is no rule to reach.

cases.name: user/enumerated-below-bulk-threshold
cases.given: three accounts, permanently — under the 20-entity broad_min.

cases.name: term/single
cases.given: one taxonomy term. wp_delete_term() has no trash.

cases.name: attachment/default-config
cases.given: one attachment with MEDIA_TRASH at its default (off): the original file and every generated size are unlinked from disk.

cases.name: option/single
cases.given: one site option deleted. delete_option() keeps no prior value.
cases.note: The note this replaces said blast_radius for a single option was an OPEN question that #94 would answer `broad`, and deliberately asserted nothing. Measured on the merged adapter, it does. Recorded now, with the measurement.
cases.closed_by: #94 (RFX-131) SETTLES the open question this row's own note recorded. `options/delete {option: ...}` enumerates no affected set, §4.2 reads that as a predicate, and a predicate is `broad` — so this is an R2 row, not the RFX-153 row it was filed as. #101 (RFX-164) supplies the irreversible: delete_option() keeps no prior value.

cases.name: plugin/files
cases.given: a plugin's files removed from disk. Nothing in WordPress restores them.
cases.note: HELD ON TWO INDEPENDENT GROUNDS, and only R2 is asserted here. Substituting irreversible/SINGLE — i.e. conceding the cardinality question entirely — still returns require_approval, under reeflex.policy/authority_change_prod (R7, #118 / RFX-128): removing a plugin's files changes what code runs. Measured, not assumed. `required` records R2 because that is the rule the shipped adapter's axes reach; the R7 floor is pinned by reeflex-core/tests/test_authority_family_rfx128.py.
cases.closed_by: Same as option/single: #94 (RFX-131) prices a call that enumerates nothing as `broad`, #101 (RFX-164) prices removed plugin files as irreversible. R2 as shipped.
